summary: The most fatigued batch so far. Commons and Uncommons are often good kitchen observation (the food processor's nine attachments, colander hat, microwave-style double beeps, the induction hob that only heats pans it likes, the lazy susan spinning the wrong way, the paella pan hanging off the hob, the oven mitt fish puppet), and some Legendaries are strong (freezer peas labelled in another alphabet, the slugs giving up, the grandad wrinkly as a raisin, the knife marks that spell a recipe, the lid that fits every pan, the pizza carried out on a door). The problems: (1) about 70 Legendaries are 'never dropped / never spilled / for thirty years / so many X that' or quiet successes, and about 14 are 'fed a whole street / village / wedding / campsite'; 109 of 112 Legendary names are 'The X That Y'; (2) Rares are often the object doing its job well; Epics are often 'made so much X for a party'; (3) one trait scaled over three or four rarities in about 20 objects (sieve flour, coffee grinder waking, garlic smell, popcorn volume, pancakes, foam, sneezing, slow-cooker smell, pet-bowl summoning, nail-clipping flinging); (4) cluster copies: exercise mat = yoga mat, kettle grill = smoker, steamer = steamer basket, three 'always full' bowls, and the heater group's 'kept everyone warm in a snowstorm' Legendaries; (5) cross-batch copies: sugar bowl dish = w20 x_sugar_bowl almost line for line, salad bowl = w15 x_salad_bowl, fruit bowl and Pilot 02 banana (ripening), popcorn maker = w15 corn, bread maker = w20 oven, sandwich toaster = w21 calzone, pie dish = w21 apple pie, crepe pan = w13 plane, boiler = w20 radiator, electric blanket = w17 throw blanket. Safety: the stove top's delayed gas 'whoomph', the toaster oven's glowing crumbs and the electric blanket left on until too hot are rewritten; the bathroom scale's weight jokes (moody numbers, 'oh dear') are moved off body weight. Knife, deep fryer and heaters are otherwise framed safely. Mechanics: most renamed moves are truthful, but default fridge kit names ('Frost Breath', 'Cold Storage', 'Ice Cube Barrage') were kept on about 25 heating and cooking appliances, and kitchen kit names ('Taste Test', 'Hot Ladle', 'Stir Up', 'Clatter') on mats, scales, clippers, tweezers, a mouse pad and a boxing glove; replacements are given. Several Ultimates repeat the Epic name (pizza oven exactly, yoga mat exactly) or carry heat/cold/rescue words that do not fit every variant. All replacements were checked by script for length, ASCII and global name uniqueness.

patterns.pattern: Cluster tell-apart. Mats: exercise mat = sit-ups and star jumps, yoga mat = poses and bending, bath mat = wet feet, doormat = WELCOME and mud, mouse pad = glide. Grills: barbecue = sausages and smoke screens, kettle grill = round beetle on legs, smoker = slow wood smoke, electric grill = indoor stripes, grill = toast under the grill. Steamers: steamer = glasses and puddings, steamer basket = sleepy dumplings and stacking, pressure cooker = hiss and speed. Bowls: bowl = depth, cat bowl = never full enough, dog bowl = slops, buries, shines, pet food bowl = trip hazard and treaties, fruit bowl = hoarding, serving bowl = passing round. patterns.pattern: Default kit names that contradict the object: fridge kit 'Frost Breath' / 'Cold Storage' / 'Ice Cube Barrage' kept on heaters, blankets, fryers, ovens, cookers and toasters; kitchen kit 'Taste Test' / 'Hot Ladle' / 'Stir Up' / 'Clatter' kept on mats, scales, clippers, tweezers, a mouse pad and a boxing glove.
patterns.suggestion: Per-slot replacements given, checked against each kit move's mechanics (defdown = crack/distract/soften, self defup = guard/lock/armour, 45% x3 = plural/repeated, heal = rest, stun = jolt/beep, burn = heat).

patterns.pattern: Ultimate names: exact or near repeats of the Epic name (pizza oven, yoga mat, fork, chopsticks, cat bowl, stove top, baking tray, pie dish, potpie) and words that misstate variants (sieve snow on a burn variant; furnace, stock pot heat words with no burn; strainer, oven mitt rescue words; heating pad soothing).

Safety and sensitivity: stove top U (delayed gas ignition 'whoomph'), toaster oven U (glowing crumbs), electric blanket U (left on until too hot), bathroom scale U/R/E (body-weight jokes for children). Knife (grown-up only, butter-knife Legendary), deep fryer (grown-ups only), gas heater, ramekin and oven mitt lines are acceptable. Wine cooler and bottle opener stay alcohol-free (no drink named).
